system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Global Order: Debt, Energy and Multi‑theater Conflict
system_description.narrative_summary: A concentrated set of interacting stresses — soaring sovereign debt and a brittle Treasury/bond market, an American turn to economic warfare (notably versus Iran) that is driving energy-price shocks, and renewed great‑power and regional military tensions — are reshaping the global order in real time. Policymakers are using unconventional fiscal and regulatory tools (Treasury buybacks, sweeping sanctions, tariff maneuvers) to buy stability, but those moves create cross‑pressures on currencies, commodity markets, and central bank policy. At the same time, strategic competition in technology and trade (AI chips, data centers, tariffs) and multiple active conflict theaters (Middle East, Ukraine, Korean Peninsula) increase the risk of cascading, system‑wide feedbacks.
system_description.scope: The open system includes sovereign states and alliances, global financial and sovereign debt markets, energy and commodity supply chains (oil, shipping routes), high‑technology and industrial supply chains (semiconductors, data centers), multilateral institutions, sanctions and trade regimes, and the major active conflict theaters and their regional spillovers.
system_description.super_system: The planetary, globalized political‑economic‑environmental system (the international order that integrates states, markets, information networks and ecological constraints).

variables.name: US–Iran strategic confrontation
variables.description: The United States, Iran and their regional partners and proxies are locked in an escalating mix of economic warfare and limited military exchanges that is shifting the contest toward sustained sanctions, coercive diplomacy and proxy pressure.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed politically and materially by Western states, are locked in a high‑intensity conflict marked by renewed missile and drone campaigns, strikes on economic infrastructure and growing weapon and air‑defence shortages that are altering battlefield dynamics and alliance burdens.

variables.name: US Treasury market stress and fiscal‑monetary tug
variables.description: A shifting balance among the U.S. Treasury, financial markets and the Federal Reserve—driven by record government debt, aggressive long‑bond buybacks and volatile yields—is reshaping market liquidity, the dollar’s role and the limits of conventional monetary policy.

variables.name: Tech and semiconductor geopolitical rivalry
variables.description: The United States, China and their partners are contesting dominance over AI chips, advanced semiconductors, data‑centre infrastructure and related export/investment controls, accelerating supply‑chain decoupling and industrial policy competition.

variables.name: North Korea nuclear‑missile standoff
variables.description: North Korea’s intensifying missile tests, growing nuclear‑weapon estimates and intermittent diplomatic overtures toward the U.S. and Seoul are producing a volatile regional standoff that forces allied deterrence recalibration and heightens escalation risks.
